entries.name: New Year's Day
entries.capsule: January 1, the first legal holiday of Minnesota's civic year; state and many local offices close.
entries.dateRule: January 1 (Gregorian). If it falls on a Saturday, the preceding Friday is the observed holiday; if Sunday, the following Monday.
entries.whatItMarks: The start of the calendar year.
entries.workplaceNote: Jan. 1, 2028 is a Saturday, so under Minn. Stat. 645.44 the observed state holiday is Friday, Dec. 31, 2027.

entries.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Day
entries.capsule: Third Monday in January; a Minnesota legal holiday marked by the annual Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Holiday Breakfast in Minneapolis.
entries.dateRule: Third Monday in January (Minn. Stat. 645.44 and federal law).

dates.source: General Mills, 36th annual Holiday Breakfast announcement

entries.whatItMarks: The birthday and legacy of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and the civil rights movement.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: General Mills and UNCF Twin Cities held the 36th annual Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Holiday Breakfast at the Minneapolis Convention Center on Jan. 19, 2026, 7:30 to 9:30 a.m., with keynotes by Soledad O'Brien and Freeman Hrabowski; colleges such as St. Olaf hold events through January. See the African American page for community observances.

minnesotaEvents.name: 36th Annual Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Holiday Breakfast
minnesotaEvents.organizerDates: Monday, Jan. 19, 2026, 7:30-9:30 a.m. (General Mills and UNCF)

entries.workplaceNote: A legal holiday under Minn. Stat. 645.44; public business is not transacted.

sources.title: General Mills and UNCF Celebrate 36th Annual Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Holiday Breakfast
2026 MLK Jr. Day, St. Olaf College

entries.name: Black History Month (begins)
entries.capsule: February, a national month for Black history; Minnesota observances are covered on the African American page.
entries.dateRule: February 1 begins the month (by custom; not a Minnesota legal holiday).

dates.source: Fixed by custom (seed); no official page opened stating the date
Fixed by custom (seed); no official page opened stating the date
Fixed by custom (seed); no official page opened stating the date

entries.whatItMarks: A national month recognizing African American history and contributions.

entries.name: Washington's and Lincoln's Birthday
entries.capsule: Third Monday in February; Minnesota law keeps the name Washington's and Lincoln's Birthday for what many call Presidents' Day.
entries.whatItMarks: The birthdays of Presidents George Washington and Abraham Lincoln.
entries.workplaceNote: A legal holiday under Minn. Stat. 645.44.

entries.name: St. Patrick's Day
entries.capsule: March 17; St. Paul's downtown parade, held since the 1960s, draws thousands of marchers, Irish and otherwise.
entries.dateRule: March 17. St. Paul's parade is held on the day itself at noon.

dates.source: MPR News report on the 60th parade

entries.whatItMarks: The feast of St. Patrick, patron saint of Ireland, now a broad celebration of Irish heritage.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: St. Paul held its 60th annual St. Patrick's Day Parade on Tuesday, March 17, 2026, from Mears Park along Fifth Street to Rice Park, led by the year's Miss Shamrock; MPR described thousands of 'green-clad Irish and Irish wannabes.' See the European American page for Irish heritage.

minnesotaEvents.name: 60th Annual St. Patrick's Day Parade
minnesotaEvents.place: Downtown St. Paul, Mears Park to Rice Park along Fifth Street
minnesotaEvents.organizerDates: Held Tuesday, March 17, 2026 (as reported by MPR News)

sources.title: Thousands march through St. Paul in 60th St. Patrick's Day parade

entries.name: Easter
entries.capsule: The main Christian feast of the resurrection; observed in Minnesota's churches but not a state legal holiday.
entries.dateRule: First Sunday after the first ecclesiastical full moon on or after March 21 (Western churches).
entries.whatItMarks: The resurrection of Jesus in Christian belief.
entries.workplaceNote: Easter is not among the legal holidays listed in Minn. Stat. 645.44.

entries.name: Memorial Day
entries.capsule: Last Monday in May; honors those who died in U.S. military service, with Minnesota's main ceremony at Fort Snelling National Cemetery.
entries.whatItMarks: Remembrance of U.S. service members who died in military service.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Fort Snelling National Cemetery and the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs hold a wreath-laying ceremony with music, speeches, a moment of silence, a rifle volley and Taps; in 2025 it began at 9:45 a.m. and the governor spoke.

minnesotaEvents.name: Memorial Day wreath-laying ceremony
minnesotaEvents.organizerDates: Monday, May 26, 2025, 9:45 a.m. (as reported); 2026 details not opened

entries.workplaceNote: A legal holiday under Minn. Stat. 645.44.

sources.title: Fort Snelling to hold wreath-laying ceremony on Memorial Day (KTTC)

entries.name: Juneteenth
entries.capsule: June 19; a Minnesota state holiday since a 2023 law marking the end of slavery in the United States.
entries.dateRule: June 19. If it falls on a Saturday the Friday before is the holiday; if Sunday, the Monday after.
entries.whatItMarks: The end of slavery in the United States.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Gov. Tim Walz signed the bill making Juneteenth a state holiday on Feb. 3, 2023. Community celebrations are covered on the African American page.
entries.workplaceNote: A legal holiday under Minn. Stat. 645.44. June 19, 2027 is a Saturday, so the observed state holiday is Friday, June 18, 2027.

sources.title: Juneteenth is now a holiday in Minnesota (MPR News)

entries.name: Independence Day (United States)
entries.capsule: July 4; parades, picnics and fireworks statewide. In 2026 Minnesota marked the nation's 250th anniversary.
entries.dateRule: July 4. If it falls on a Saturday the Friday before is the holiday; if Sunday, the Monday after.
entries.whatItMarks: The Declaration of Independence of 1776 and the founding of the United States.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Cities hold parades, concerts and fireworks, from the Minneapolis Park Board's Red, White and Boom! on the riverfront to hometown celebrations in Delano, Ely, Stillwater, St. Cloud and Rochester. For the 250th in 2026, Historic Fort Snelling and the Oliver Kelley Farm held historical celebrations, Mall of America hosted a free America 250 exhibit, and the State Capitol held a public reading of the Declaration on July 8.

minnesotaEvents.name: Red, White and Boom!
minnesotaEvents.place: Water Works Park and West River Parkway, Minneapolis
minnesotaEvents.organizerDates: Saturday, July 4, 2026 (Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board, as listed)

minnesotaEvents.name: Minnesota America 250 exhibit and recognition
minnesotaEvents.place: Huntington Bank Rotunda, Mall of America, Bloomington
minnesotaEvents.organizerDates: July 3-5, 2026; recognition ceremony July 4, 11 a.m. (Dakota County Historical Society)

minnesotaEvents.name: Sharing the Spirit of America: Nationwide Reading of the Declaration of Independence
minnesotaEvents.place: Minnesota State Capitol Rotunda, St. Paul
minnesotaEvents.organizerDates: July 8, 2026, 5-6:30 p.m. (Governor's Committee for Minnesota America 250 and MNHS)

entries.workplaceNote: July 4, 2026 fell on a Saturday, so the observed state holiday was Friday, July 3 (Minn. Stat. 645.44); MPR noted many people had that Friday off. July 4, 2027 is a Sunday, so Monday, July 5, 2027 is observed.

entries.name: Minnesota State Fair
entries.capsule: Twelve days ending on Labor Day at Falcon Heights: livestock, 4-H, food, art and nearly 2 million visitors.
entries.dateRule: The 12 days ending on Labor Day, set by the Minnesota State Fair.

dates.source: KTTC report of the fair's announced 2027 start

entries.whatItMarks: Minnesota's agricultural and community fair, held since 1859 and on its permanent grounds since 1885.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: In 2026 the fair ran Aug. 27 to Sept. 7 and drew 1,923,325 people. It featured more than 38,000 competition entries, the 4-H Purple Ribbon Auction, the state's largest juried art show and the crowning of Princess Kay of the Milky Way.

sources.title: Minnesota State Fair draws 1.9 million visitors in 2026 (KTTC)
Minnesota State Fair: Origins and Traditions (MNopedia)

entries.name: Labor Day
entries.capsule: First Monday in September; honors workers, closes the State Fair, and in most districts precedes the first day of school.

dates.source: Minnesota State Fair (Labor Day attendance on its final day, Sept. 7, 2026)

entries.whatItMarks: The contributions of working people and the labor movement.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Labor Day is the last day of the State Fair. From 1900 to 1910 about 30,000 people joined St. Paul's Labor Day parade and Harriet Island picnic each year, MNopedia records. State law bars most public school districts from starting the school year before Labor Day.
entries.workplaceNote: A legal holiday under Minn. Stat. 645.44; Minn. Stat. 120A.40 bars most districts from starting school before Labor Day.

sources.title: Labor and Labor Organizing in Minnesota (MNopedia)

entries.name: Indigenous Peoples Day
alsoKnownAs: formerly Columbus Day in Minnesota law
entries.capsule: Second Monday in October, named in Minnesota law; the state executive branch does not close that day.
entries.whatItMarks: As named in Minnesota statute. Observances belong to Tribal Nations and are not described here.
entries.workplaceNote: Minn. Stat. 645.44 lists it as a holiday but excludes it for the state executive branch; other branches and local governments decide for themselves, and public-employer contracts naming Columbus Day must cite Indigenous Peoples Day.

entries.name: Halloween
entries.capsule: October 31; costumes and trick-or-treating, with Anoka, the self-styled Halloween Capital of the World, holding parades since 1920.
entries.dateRule: October 31. Anoka's Grande Day Parade is set each year by Anoka Halloween Inc., usually on a Saturday before the 31st.

dates.source: Fixed by custom; no official page opened stating the date
Fixed by custom; no official page opened stating the date
Fixed by custom; no official page opened stating the date

entries.whatItMarks: The eve of All Saints' Day, now a broad secular festival.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Anoka Halloween Inc. says Anoka civic clubs organized a citywide celebration in 1920 to divert young people from pranks. The 2026 Grande Day Parade ran on Anoka's Main Street on Oct. 24, 1-3:30 p.m.

entries.name: Election Day (general election)
entries.capsule: First Tuesday after the first Monday in November in even years; Minnesota workers may take paid time to vote.
entries.dateRule: State general elections fall on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of even-numbered years; odd years hold only local elections.

dates.source: KAXE report on the Nov. 3, 2026 election
Calculated: first Tuesday after the first Monday in November

entries.whatItMarks: Voting for federal, state and local offices.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Minnesota had 76.35 percent turnout in 2024. By Oct. 16, 2026, officials had accepted 202,252 absentee ballots, 17 percent above the same point in 2022.
entries.workplaceNote: Minn. Stat. 204C.04 lets employees leave work to vote, on Election Day or during in-person early voting, without penalty or loss of pay.

sources.title: Early voting opens in MN midterms (KAXE)
Minnesota leads US in voter turnout for 2024 election (KEYC)

entries.name: Firearms deer season opener
entries.capsule: Early November Saturday when hundreds of thousands of Minnesotans head out deer hunting with family and friends.
entries.dateRule: Set by the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources each year, on a Saturday in early November.
entries.whatItMarks: The start of the firearms deer hunting season.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: The DNR expected more than 400,000 hunters for the Nov. 7, 2026 opener and describes it as a time of memories with friends and family outdoors. It matters most in Greater Minnesota; see the rural page.

sources.title: Minnesota DNR provides deer hunting outlook and regulation reminders

entries.name: Veterans Day
entries.capsule: November 11; honors all who served in the U.S. armed forces, with the state's official program in Inver Grove Heights.
entries.dateRule: November 11. If it falls on a Saturday the Friday before is the holiday; if Sunday, the Monday after.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: The state's official Veterans Day program has been held in Inver Grove Heights with a breakfast for veterans and families and music by the 34th Infantry Division Red Bull Band. Minnesota has about 295,703 veterans.
entries.workplaceNote: A legal holiday under Minn. Stat. 645.44; public-employer contracts must cite Nov. 11. Nov. 11, 2028 is a Saturday, so Friday, Nov. 10, 2028 is observed.

sources.title: Hundreds Gather At State Veterans Day Program (CBS Minnesota)

entries.name: Thanksgiving
entries.capsule: Fourth Thursday in November; a family harvest meal, often turkey, from the nation's top turkey-producing state.
entries.dateRule: Fourth Thursday in November (Minn. Stat. 645.44). The state executive branch also closes the Friday after.
entries.whatItMarks: A national day of thanks, centered on a family meal.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Each year the governor receives an official Thanksgiving turkey at the Capitol with the Minnesota Turkey Growers Association, honoring the state's more than 600 turkey farms; Minnesota raised 32.0 million turkeys in 2025, the most of any state.
entries.workplaceNote: A legal holiday under Minn. Stat. 645.44; for the state executive branch the Friday after Thanksgiving is also a holiday, and other public bodies may choose.

sources.title: Minnesota turkey showcased at the State Capitol (WDIO)

entries.name: Christmas
entries.capsule: December 25; a Christian feast and the year's biggest family and shopping holiday, a Minnesota legal holiday.
entries.dateRule: December 25. If it falls on a Saturday the Friday before is the holiday; if Sunday, the Monday after.
entries.whatItMarks: The birth of Jesus in Christian belief; also a broad civic and family holiday.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Congregations hold services; public light displays include Duluth's Bentleyville Tour of Lights, which runs Nov. 21 to Dec. 26, 2026.
entries.workplaceNote: A legal holiday under Minn. Stat. 645.44. Dec. 25, 2027 is a Saturday, so Friday, Dec. 24, 2027 is observed.
